schema of the entity changes (e.g. new fields are added), allowing the node to
deserialize entries written under earlier formats.

compositeHash.description:
Composite hash derived from sourceAddress, targetAddress, scopedMetadataKey, targetId, and metadataType.
It uniquely identifies the metadata entry.

sourceAddress.description: Hex-encoded address of the account that created the metadata entry.

targetAddress.description:
Hex-encoded address of the target account.
For mosaic metadata and namespace metadata, this is the address of the resource owner.

scopedMetadataKey.description: 64-bit key assigned by the metadata creator to identify the metadata entry within the source and target context.

targetId.description: Mosaic or namespace identifier for mosaic metadata or namespace metadata. For account metadata, this value is 0.

anyOf.description:
Unique [mosaic](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/mosaic.html) identifier.
A 64-bit unsigned integer derived from the creator's address and a registration nonce,
encoded as a 16-character hexadecimal string.

Unique [namespace](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/namespaces.html) identifier.
A 64-bit unsigned integer derived from the namespace name and its parent namespace ID,
encoded as a 16-character hexadecimal string.

metadataType.description:

- `0`: Account metadata
- `1`: Mosaic metadata
- `2`: Namespace metadata

valueSize.description: Size of the metadata value in bytes.

value.description:
Metadata value encoded as hex.
In metadata transactions, this field contains the new value when no previous value exists.
When updating existing metadata, it contains the byte-wise XOR of the previous value and the new value.

get.description: Returns the Merkle proof for the metadata state entry associated with the given composite hash.

parameters.name: compositeHash
parameters.description: Composite hash encoded as a 64-character hexadecimal string.

schema.description: 256-bit hash encoded as a 64-character hexadecimal string.

200.description: Merkle proof for the requested metadata state entry.

schema.description: The Merkle path information clients can use to prove the state of the given entity.

raw.description:
Serialized Patricia Merkle tree in compact hex format, as returned by the server.
Used for [state proofs](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/data-validation.html) to verify
entity state (account, mosaic, metadata, etc.) without downloading the full ledger.
See [Symbol Technical Reference](https://symbol.github.io/symbol-technicalref/main.pdf)
chapter 4.3 for the tree structure specification.

tree.description: Merkle tree parsed from Merkle tree raw.

anyOf.description:
Internal node of a [Patricia Merkle tree](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/data-validation.html)
used in state proofs. A branch has up to 16 child links (one per nibble 0 to F) and a path prefix.

type.description: Node type (always branch).

path.description: Path prefix (hex) from root to this branch.

nibbleCount.description: Number of nibbles in the path.

linkMask.description: Bitmask indicating which nibble slots (0 to 15) have child links.

items.description:
Child link in a [Merkle tree branch](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/data-validation.html)
node. Each link points to a child node (branch or leaf) via its hash.

bit.description: Nibble index (0 to 15) identifying this child slot (hex).

anyOf.description:
Terminal node of a [Patricia Merkle tree](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/data-validation.html)
used in state proofs. A leaf stores the final path and the associated value (entity state hash).

type.description: Node type (always leaf).

path.description: Full path (hex) from root to this leaf.

nibbleCount.description: Number of nibbles in the path.

value.description: Leaf value (SHA3-256 hash of the entity state).

get.description:
Returns the decoded binary payload stored in Metal metadata entries identified by the given metal id.
Metal is a convention for storing chunked binary payloads in metadata entries. See the
[metal-on-symbol repository](https://github.com/OPENSPHERE-Inc/metal-on-symbol).
The response content type is derived from the stored Metal seal when available, or defaults to
`application/octet-stream`. Optional query parameters can override the response headers for
content type and filename.

parameters.name: metalId
parameters.description: Metal identifier: Base58-encoded composite hash of the first metadata chunk.

parameters.name: mimeType
parameters.description: Override the MIME type of the response.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: Override the filename in the Content-Disposition header.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: When true, sets Content-Disposition to attachment.

200.description: Binary payload of the Metal metadata.

Content-Disposition.description:
Indicates whether the payload is returned inline or as an attachment and, when available,
includes the resolved filename.

Content-MetalText.description:
Original decoded Metal seal text associated with the payload, when the payload was stored
with a Metal seal.

get.description:
Retrieves the current on-chain state for a mosaic.
The response includes the mosaic definition, such as supply, divisibility, owner address, duration, and behavior flags.

parameters.name: mosaicId
parameters.description: Mosaic identifier encoded as a 16-character hexadecimal string.

schema.description:
Unique [mosaic](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/mosaic.html) identifier.
A 64-bit unsigned integer derived from the creator's address and a registration nonce,
encoded as a 16-character hexadecimal string.
Mosaic information including an internal resource identifier and the full mosaic state.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the object in the node's database (MongoDB ObjectId).
Used as the ``offset`` parameter value for cursor-based pagination.

mosaic.description: State information describing a mosaic definition.

version.description:
Version of the on-chain state serialization format. Incremented when the storage
schema of the entity changes (e.g. new fields are added), allowing the node to
deserialize entries written under earlier formats.

id.description:
Unique [mosaic](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/mosaic.html) identifier.
A 64-bit unsigned integer derived from the creator's address and a registration nonce,
encoded as a 16-character hexadecimal string.

supply.description: Current total supply of the mosaic, expressed in the smallest (atomic) unit.

startHeight.description: Block height at which the mosaic became active.

ownerAddress.description: Address of the account that created the mosaic.

revision.description:
Revision number of the mosaic definition.
Starts at 1 when the mosaic is created and increments each time the same mosaic definition is modified.

flags.description:
Mosaic flags bitmask. Individual values can be combined.
- 0x00 (0 decimal): No flags present.
- 0x01 (1 decimal, `supplyMutable`): Mosaic supply can be increased or decreased later.
- 0x02 (2 decimal, `transferable`): Mosaic can be transferred between arbitrary accounts.
  When not set, it can only be transferred to and from the mosaic owner.
- 0x04 (4 decimal, `restrictable`): Mosaic supports custom restrictions configured by the mosaic owner.
- 0x08 (8 decimal, `revokable`): Mosaic creator can revoke balances from another account.

Example: `3` means `0x01 + 0x02`, so the mosaic is both `supplyMutable` and `transferable`.

divisibility.description:
Determines up to what decimal place a mosaic can be divided.
Divisibility of 3 means that a mosaic can be divided into smallest parts of 0.001 mosaics.
The divisibility must be in the range of 0 and 6.

duration.description: Duration of the mosaic in blocks. A value of 0 indicates a non-expiring mosaic.

Clients can use this information to verify that the mosaic state is included in the node's state Merkle tree.
If the supplied mosaic ID does not exist, the endpoint still returns a Merkle proof response,
but it is a negative proof showing that no mosaic state entry exists for the requested mosaic ID.
See [Data Validation](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/data-validation.html) for an overview of Patricia Merkle
trees and state proofs on Symbol.

Revision number of the mosaic definition.
Starts at 1 when the mosaic is created and increments each time the same mosaic definition is modified.

flags.description:
Mosaic flags bitmask. Individual values can be combined.
- 0x00 (0 decimal): No flags present.
- 0x01 (1 decimal, `supplyMutable`): Mosaic supply can be increased or decreased later.
- 0x02 (2 decimal, `transferable`): Mosaic can be transferred between arbitrary accounts.
  When not set, it can only be transferred to and from the mosaic owner.
- 0x04 (4 decimal, `restrictable`): Mosaic supports custom restrictions configured by the mosaic owner.
- 0x08 (8 decimal, `revokable`): Mosaic creator can revoke balances from another account.

Example: `3` means `0x01 + 0x02`, so the mosaic is both `supplyMutable` and `transferable`.

divisibility.description:
Determines up to what decimal place a mosaic can be divided.
Divisibility of 3 means that a mosaic can be divided into smallest parts of 0.001 mosaics.
The divisibility must be in the range of 0 and 6.

duration.description: Duration of the mosaic in blocks. A value of 0 indicates a non-expiring mosaic.

get.description:
Returns the current multisig state for an account.

The response includes the approval thresholds for the multisig account, its direct cosignatories,
and the multisig accounts where the queried account is itself acting as a cosignatory.

If the queried account is only a cosignatory, the endpoint still returns `200`, with
`minApproval = 0`, `minRemoval = 0`, an empty `cosignatoryAddresses` array, and the related
multisig accounts listed in `multisigAddresses`.

If the account is neither a multisig account nor a cosignatory of any multisig account, the
endpoint returns `404`.

with even a single altered character will be rejected.

get.description:
Returns the [Merkle proof](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/data-validation.html#merkle-proof)
for the multisig state entry associated with the requested account.

If the requested account is a cosignatory, the endpoint returns the Merkle proof for that
account's multisig state entry. Cosignatory-only accounts still have a multisig state entry with
`minApproval = 0`, `minRemoval = 0`, an empty `cosignatoryAddresses` array, and
`multisigAddresses` listing the multisig accounts they can cosign.

If the requested account is itself a multisig account, the endpoint returns the Merkle proof for
that multisig account state entry.

If the requested account is neither a multisig account nor a cosignatory, the endpoint still
returns a Merkle proof response, but it is a negative proof showing that no multisig state entry
exists for the supplied address.

get.description:
Returns the multisig graph centered on the requested account.

Level `0` contains the requested account. Negative levels contain multisig accounts for which the
queried account acts as a cosignatory. Positive levels contain multisig relationships discovered
through the queried account's cosignatories.

If the requested account is a cosignatory but is not itself managed as a multisig account, the
response still includes level `0` for that account. In this case, the level `0` entry has
`minApproval = 0`, `minRemoval = 0`, an empty `cosignatoryAddresses` array, and
`multisigAddresses` listing the multisig accounts it can cosign.

If the requested account is neither a multisig account nor a cosignatory of any multisig account,
no multisig state entry exists for it and the endpoint returns `404`.

If the requested account is itself a multisig account, the response includes its multisig state at
level `0` together with any reachable negative and positive graph levels.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
Cursor for pagination. Provide the value of the sort field (`orderBy`) from the
last entry of the previous page. **The offset type must match `orderBy`:**
- `orderBy=id`: use the entry's `id` (ObjectId, 24-char hex).
- `orderBy=height`: use the block height (string, e.g. `"17592"`).
- `orderBy=balance`: use the mosaic balance amount (string, e.g. `"1000000"`).

Allowed `orderBy` values depend on the endpoint. If `orderBy` is omitted, `id` is used by default.

Set `offset` to the sort-field value of the last entry from the previous page. Across pages,
this value decreases with `order=desc` and increases with `order=asc`.

tags.name: Account routes
tags.description:
Accounts are the central entities on the Symbol blockchain. An
[account](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/account.html) is a key pair (private and public key)
associated with a mutable state stored on-chain. Each account is uniquely identified by an
[**address**](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/cryptography.html#address) derived from its public key,
encoded in Base32 format (39 characters). The **public key** is recorded on-chain with the first issued transaction
and remains empty until then.

An account's on-chain state includes its **balance** (the set of
[mosaic](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/mosaic.html) units it owns) and an
[**importance score**](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/consensus-algorithm.html#importance-calculation)
that determines the probability of being selected to harvest the next block. Importance is recalculated
periodically using **activity buckets**, which are rolling data that tracks fees paid, beneficiary counts, and raw
scores over a sliding window of recalculation periods.

Accounts participate in block creation through
[harvesting](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/harvesting.html). An eligible account (one that meets the
minimum balance threshold) can harvest directly, or it can
[delegate harvesting](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/harvesting.html#delegated-harvesting) to a
**remote account** (proxy) that signs blocks on its behalf. The **account type** field reflects this
relationship:
- `0`: Unlinked account, not participating in harvesting delegation.
- `1`: Balance-holding account (harvester) that is linked to a remote proxy account.
- `2`: Remote proxy account that signs blocks on behalf of a linked balance-holding account.
- `3`: Remote-harvester-eligible account that is currently unlinked.

To enable [remote](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/harvesting.html#remote-harvesting) or
[delegated](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/harvesting.html#delegated-harvesting) harvesting, the main
account links a set of **supplemental public keys**:
- `Linked key`: public key of the remote proxy account
  ([AccountKeyLinkTransaction](https://docs.symbol.dev/serialization/index.html#accountkeylinktransaction)).
- `Node key`: public key used for TLS sessions with the node
  ([NodeKeyLinkTransaction](https://docs.symbol.dev/serialization/index.html#nodekeylinktransaction));
  required only for delegated harvesting.
- `VRF key`: key used to randomize harvester selection
  ([VrfKeyLinkTransaction](https://docs.symbol.dev/serialization/index.html#vrfkeylinktransaction));
  required for all harvesting types.
- `Voting keys`: keys used for block
  [finalization](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/block.html#finalization) voting
  ([VotingKeyLinkTransaction](https://docs.symbol.dev/serialization/index.html#votingkeylinktransaction));
  each key is valid for a defined range of finalization epochs.

tags.name: Block routes
tags.description:
[Blocks](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/block.html) are the units of the Symbol blockchain. Each block
contains a list of confirmed [transactions](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/transaction.html) and is signed
by a [harvester](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/harvesting.html) account selected by the
[consensus algorithm](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/consensus-algorithm.html).

- `Height`: unique, sequential position of the block in the chain. Subsequent blocks differ in height by 1.
- `Timestamp`: number of milliseconds elapsed since the creation of the first block.
- `Difficulty`: block difficulty (initial 1e14); adjusted in range 1e13 to 1e15 to maintain target block time.
- `Harvester`: [account](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/account.html) that created the block; receives
  transaction [fees](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/fees.html) and
  [inflation](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/inflation.html) rewards.
- `Beneficiary address`: optional account designated by the harvester to receive a
  [the block reward](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/harvesting.html#rewards).
- `Fee multiplier`: multiplier applied to transaction size to calculate the
  [effective fee](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/fees.html).
- `Importance block`: a special block type that additionally records voting-eligible account count,
  harvesting-eligible account count, total voting balance, and the previous importance block hash.
- `Finalization` ([docs](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/block.html#finalization)): the process that makes blocks
  permanent. Once a block is finalized, its transactions become immutable. Clients that rely on immutability
  should only trust finalized blocks.

tags.name: Chain routes
tags.description:
Chain endpoints provide aggregate information about the blockchain state.
The [chain score](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/block.html) is used during synchronization:
nodes select the chain with the highest score as the canonical one (higher = better chain).
The [latest finalized block](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/block.html#finalization) is the most recent
block that has been made permanent and will never be rolled back.

tags.name: Finalization routes
tags.description:
[Finalization](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/block.html#finalization) is the process that makes
blocks permanent on the Symbol blockchain. Once a block is finalized, its transactions become
immutable and will never be rolled back.

Finalization occurs in rounds called **epochs** (e.g. every 1440 blocks, ~12h on mainnet).
Each epoch is divided into **finalization points**. Voters (eligible accounts with linked voting keys)
emit prevote and precommit messages; when more than 67% of the voting stake agrees, the block
is finalized.

These endpoints return the **finalization proof** which is cryptographic evidence that a block was
finalized, including message groups (prevote, precommit, count stages) and BLS aggregate
signatures from the voter set.

tags.name: Metadata routes
tags.description:
[Metadata](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/metadata.html) lets accounts attach arbitrary key-value
data to three kinds of on-chain resources on Symbol: **accounts**, **mosaics**, and **namespaces**.
Each metadata entry is uniquely identified by its source address, target address, metadata type,
scoped metadata key, and, for mosaic and namespace metadata, the target artifact id. The derived
composite hash can be used as a compact identifier for lookup.

- `Source address`: account that created the metadata update.
- `Target address`: target account for account metadata, or the owner account for mosaic and namespace metadata.
- `Scoped metadata key`: 64-bit key assigned by the metadata creator to distinguish metadata entries.
- `Metadata type`: whether the metadata entry is attached to an account, mosaic, or namespace.
- `Composite hash`: unique identifier derived from the metadata coordinates.
- `Metal`: convention for storing chunked binary payloads in metadata entries. See the
  [metal-on-symbol repository](https://github.com/OPENSPHERE-Inc/metal-on-symbol).

Metadata endpoints return individual metadata entries, batch lookup results, paginated search
results, Merkle proofs for metadata state, and decoded binary payloads stored with the Metal
convention.

tags.name: Mosaic routes
tags.description:
[Mosaics](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/mosaic.html) are customizable blockchain assets on Symbol.
A mosaic definition specifies its unique identifier, total supply, divisibility, owner, duration, and behavior flags.

- `Mosaic ID`: unique identifier of a mosaic on Symbol.
- `Mosaic definition`: on-chain state that describes the mosaic supply, divisibility, owner, duration, and flags.
- `Supply`: total number of mosaic units in existence, expressed in the smallest indivisible / atomic unit.
- `Divisibility`: number of decimal places supported by the mosaic, from 0 to 6.
- `Duration`: number of blocks for which the mosaic remains active. A value of `0` means the mosaic does not expire.
- `Flags`: behavior settings that control supply mutability, transferability, restrictability, and revocability.
- `Alias`: namespace alias that can be used to refer to the mosaic instead of its raw mosaic ID.

The behavior flags determine whether the mosaic supply can change, whether it can be transferred between arbitrary
accounts, whether custom restrictions can be applied, and whether the creator can revoke balances from holders.

Mosaic endpoints return mosaic definitions, paginated mosaic collections, and Merkle proofs for mosaic state.

tags.name: Multisig routes
tags.description:
[Multisig accounts](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/multisig-account.html) require approvals
from one or more cosignatories before they can act. Symbol uses an **M-of-N** model, where
`N` is the number of cosignatories attached to the multisig account and `M` is the minimum
number of approvals required for a given action.

Symbol also supports **multi-level multisig**, where a multisig account can itself act as a
cosignatory for another multisig account, up to the network-defined maximum depth
(`multisig.maxMultisigDepth = 3` on mainnet and testnet).

- `Cosignatory`: account that manages a multisig account and can approve aggregate transactions on its behalf.
- `Minimum approval`: number of cosignatory approvals required to approve a transaction initiated by the multisig account.
- `Minimum removal`: number of cosignatory approvals required to remove a cosignatory from the multisig account.

These endpoints return the current multisig state for an account, the surrounding multisig graph
across multiple levels, and the Merkle proof for the stored multisig state.

tags.name: Namespace routes
tags.description:
[Namespaces](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/namespace.html) are human-readable names that can represent accounts,
mosaics, or hierarchical naming paths on Symbol. A namespace can be either a **root namespace** or a
**subnamespace**, and each level is identified by its own namespace ID.

- `Fully-qualified namespace name`: full dot-separated namespace path, for example `symbol.xym`.
- `Root namespace`: top-level namespace with no parent.
- `Subnamespace`: child namespace registered under another namespace.
- `Parent namespace`: direct namespace above a subnamespace in the hierarchy.
- `Duration`: number of blocks for which the namespace remains active, represented by its lifetime on-chain.
- `Alias`: link from a namespace to an account address or mosaic ID.
- `Namespace ID`: unique identifier derived from the namespace path and level.
- `Active namespace`: namespace whose lifetime includes the current chain height.

Namespaces can be linked as aliases to an account address or a mosaic ID, making on-chain identifiers easier for
humans to recognize. Namespace state also tracks owner, lifetime, hierarchy depth, and whether the namespace is
currently active.

Namespace endpoints return namespace information, alias name resolution for accounts and mosaics, paginated
namespace collections, and Merkle proofs for namespace state.

tags.name: Network routes
tags.description:
Network endpoints expose configuration and economic parameters of the Symbol blockchain.
They return **network properties** (identifier, nemesis keys, epoch adjustment),
**chain properties** (block timing, fees, limits), and **plugin properties** (per-feature settings).
Additional endpoints provide **currency supply** (total, max, circulating), **inflation** rewards
at given block heights, **rental fees** for namespaces and mosaics, and **transaction fees**
(average, median, min/max multipliers).

tags.name: Node routes
tags.description:
Node endpoints return information about the specific REST node you are connected to.
They include **node identity** (public key, roles, host, port), **server version**,
**health status**, **storage statistics** (blocks, transactions, accounts),
**node time** (for transaction deadline calculation), **unlocked accounts** (harvesting),
**connected peers**, and **node metadata** (deployment tool, version).

tags.name: Restriction Mosaic routes
tags.description:
[Mosaic restrictions](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/mosaic-restriction.html) define rule
sets that control how a mosaic can be transferred on Symbol. They are commonly used with
restrictable mosaics to enforce compliance or access rules.
Mosaic restrictions are stored as two entry types: global restrictions and address restrictions.

- `Global restriction`: the rule defined for a mosaic. It says what restriction key is checked,
  what value is expected, and how the comparison is performed.
- `Address restriction`: the value assigned to one specific account for a given mosaic and
  restriction key.

A global restriction defines the rule, and an address restriction provides the account-specific
value that is checked against that rule.

- `Restriction key`: 64-bit identifier that links related global and address restrictions.
- `Entry type`: tells whether the returned entry is a global restriction entry or an
  address-specific restriction entry.

Restriction mosaic endpoints return individual restriction entries, batch lookup results,
paginated search results, and Merkle proofs for mosaic restriction state.

tags.name: Restriction Account routes
tags.description:
[Account restrictions](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/account-restriction.html) define
rule sets that limit which transactions an account can send to or receive from other accounts
on Symbol. Depending on the applied restriction flags, these rules can allow or block incoming
transactions from specific addresses, incoming transactions containing specific mosaic IDs,
outgoing transactions to specific addresses, and outgoing transactions of specific transaction
types.

Restriction account endpoints return individual account restriction entries, batch lookup
results, paginated search results, and Merkle proofs for account restriction state.

tags.name: Receipt routes
tags.description:
[Receipts](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/receipt.html) are records produced while confirmed
transactions change blockchain state. They are grouped into **transaction statements** and
**resolution statements**.

- `Transaction statement`: groups the receipts emitted for a specific transaction source at a given
  block height, including balance transfers, balance changes, expirations, and inflation.
- `Resolution statement`: records how an unresolved namespace alias used in a transaction was
  resolved to a concrete address or mosaic ID for a specific source and block.
- `Receipt type`: numeric code identifying the kind of receipt returned in a transaction statement.
- `Source`: pointer to the transaction and, when relevant, aggregate subtransaction that produced
  the receipt or resolution entry.

Receipt endpoints return paginated statement collections that can be filtered by height and other
receipt-specific criteria. [Merkle proofs](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/data-validation.html#merkle-proof)
for receipt statements are available under Block routes.

tags.name: Transaction status routes
tags.description:
Transaction status endpoints return the current processing state of a transaction identified by its hash.
They are useful after announcing a transaction and when tracking whether it is still **unconfirmed**,
already **confirmed**, waiting as **partial**, or has **failed** validation.

These endpoints support single-hash lookup and batch lookup by transaction hashes.

tags.name: Hash Lock routes
tags.description:
[Hash locks](https://docs.symbol.dev/concepts/aggregate-transaction.html#aggregate-bonded) are temporary
deposits locked before announcing an aggregate bonded transaction. They act as an anti-spam mechanism:
the lock must be confirmed before the aggregate bonded transaction can be announced, and the locked funds
are returned when the aggregate bonded transaction completes.

Hash lock endpoints return individual lock entries, paginated lock collections, batch lookup results,
and Merkle proofs for hash lock state.

tags.name: Secret Lock routes
tags.description:
[Secret locks](https://docs.symbol.dev/guides/secretlock/index.html) temporarily lock
mosaics for a recipient until either a matching proof is announced or the lock expires.
They are used for hash-time-locked workflows such as cross-chain swaps and other conditional
transfers.

Each secret lock is identified by a composite hash and includes the owner account, recipient
account, locked mosaic and amount, hash algorithm, secret, end height, and lock status.

Secret lock endpoints return individual lock entries, paginated lock collections, batch lookup
results, and Merkle proofs for secret lock state.
